mission_08: Energy-efficient AI inference is critical for edge deployment and sustainability. Energy consumption comes from three sources: compute (MAC operations), memory access (SRAM/DRAM reads/writes), and data movement (off-chip communication is 100x more expensive than on-chip). Quantization reduces energy by using lower-precision arithmetic (8-bit MACs use 18x less energy than 32-bit). Sparsity skips zero-valued computations, saving energy proportionally to the sparsity ratio. The energy-accuracy trade-off must be optimized: lower precision saves energy but may reduce accuracy. In this mission, you implement an energy model based on Horowitz's energy costs, a quantization optimizer that finds the lowest precision meeting accuracy thresholds, and a sparsity optimizer with both unstructured and structured pruning that computes energy savings from skipped MAC operations.
